boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Camp Alleghany record (December 13, 1861) in Operations in Western Virginia [June-December 1861]. The December 12 skirmish at Camp Baxter and the Union return to Cheat Mountain are context. Campaign-wide movements, reinforcements, returns and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. Jones says his column was about 700 and the enemy about 2,500 with nine guns. Johnson reports not less than 5,000 attackers against about 1,200 effective on December 13; on December 19 he says fully 2,000 attacked his right, met by not over 300 and later 500 of his men, and gives 5,000 in all against not over 1,200 effective of all arms.
claims.rationale: Column and flank figures and each commander's estimate of the other; no return inspected. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: Jones says his column climbed a very steep and rocky mountain for about a mile to the summit on the right and rear of the camp. Johnson says there were no defenses on the right and a hastily dug trench on the left hill where his artillery stood, adding that his works had been suspended under recent orders; NPS says Johnson occupied the summit to defend the Staunton-Parkersburg Pike.
claims.rationale: Ground from the two reports and a summary; no map inspected.

claims.value: The frozen and live commanders are Colonel Edward Johnson and Brigadier General Robert Milroy. Johnson says Reynolds commanded the whole Union force and Milroy the attack on his right; Jones's report is addressed to Milroy and follows his directions. Milroy's own report is not in the inspected pages.
claims.rationale: Command roles from the two reports; no automatic sole credit.

claims.value: The frozen and live casualty fields read 283 (US 137; CS 146). Johnson gives his losses as 20 killed, 96 wounded and 28 missing, many of the missing since returned, and says the enemy left 35 dead and 13 wounded on the field and he took 3 prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Johnson's 144 differs from the frozen Confederate 146; the Union return printed with Milroy's papers was read but not selected.

open_questions: Milroy's own report is marked not found in Volume V; his No. 1 papers (a relayed telegram, a record-of-events extract and the Union casualty return) were read but not selected under the three-family ceiling. Loring's reports, Benjamin's letter and the Confederate subordinate reports and return (Nos. 6-10) remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Jones's December 13, 1861 report to Milroy (Official Records Series I, Volume V) is one family of interested Union accounts. Edward Johnson's December 13, 15 and 19, 1861 reports (same volume) are one family of interested Confederate accounts. The Official Records volumes are shared containers, not additional witnesses. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge. No Scribner Campaigns of the Civil War volume narrates this engagement; Nicolay's Chapter XII ends with McClellan's campaign in July.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
